title: How a session is assigned to an App Connector

prose.text: Which connector a session lands on, and what a missing or zero connector in the logs means.

checks.do: The user's location, the connector's group location and the connector-to-application latency, rather than distance alone.
Whether the user's last request to the application was within 15 minutes, which pins them to the same connector.

closest-by-location-and-latency.statement: Private Access selects the closest App Connector given the location of the user and the App Connector-to-application latency.

quotes: Private Access selects the closest App Connector given the location of the user and the App Connector-to-application latency.
Private Access (ZPA) selects the closest App Connector given the location of the user and the App Connector-to-application latency.

nearest-is-not-geography-alone.statement: Because latency to the application is an input, the geographically nearest connector is not necessarily the one selected.
nearest-is-not-geography-alone.conditions: Inference from the two named inputs; no source gives a case of a farther connector being chosen.

group-location-feeds-path-selection.statement: The location set on the App Connector group is used in application path selection.

quotes: Configure the preferred local version profile for associated App Connectors and the App Connector’s location used in application path selection.

affinity-15-minutes.statement: Private Access keeps an active user on the same App Connector for 15 minutes after the user's last request to the application; the timer starts at selection and refreshes on each request.

quotes: Private Access maintains App Connector affinity for an active user for 15 minutes following the user's last application request.
The 15-minute timer starts at selection. If the user continues accessing the same application, the timer refreshes on each request

affinity-rebalance.statement: If a connector's load exceeds 70% and the load difference between connectors is greater than 20%, the system might reevaluate affinity and shift traffic to a different connector.

quotes: However, if an App Connector's load exceeds 70% and the load difference between App Connectors is greater than 20%, the system might reevaluate App Connector affinity and shift traffic to a different App Connector.

uneven-load-expected.statement: Load (interface statistics) is not always split equally between connectors in a group; the Health Dashboard shows how applications are split between them over a period.

quotes: Sometimes the load (i.e., the interface stats) is not equally split between the App Connectors in the App Connector group.
You can check the Health Dashboard to help you address your questions about App Connector load balance and to see the application split between App Connectors in a given period of time.

connector-id-zero.statement: Logs and diagnostics show the App Connector ID as zero when the Central Authority cannot determine the application or resolve the connection to a connector; this occurs for the session status codes APP_NOT_REACHABLE, INVALID_DOMAIN and NO_CONNECTOR_AVAILABLE.

quotes: If the Central Authority cannot determine an application or resolve the connection to the App Connector for the user, it displays the App Connector ID as zero.

segment-prefers-nearest-connector.statement: Application segments carry a boolean selectConnectorCloseToApp, documented in the Python SDK as 'Prefer nearest connector routing'.

browser-access-closest-responds.statement: For Browser Access, the Service Edge asks the App Connectors at the application level and the connector closest to the internal web application responds by connecting to it.

quotes: the App Connector sitting closest to the internal web application responds by connecting to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge.
When the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge sends out a request to all App Connectors sitting at the application level

latency-probe-cadence.title: Latency measurement cadence
latency-probe-cadence.detail: Tracked as legacy ledger item zpa-27. Unverified legacy statement: "ZPA picks by app-to-connector latency from continuous Zscaler-side measurements (not static geography)." No source states how often connector-to-application latency is measured or how long a network path change takes to be noticed.

eligibility-filter.title: Eligibility filter before latency selection
eligibility-filter.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "ZPA's connector-selection step happens in two phases - eligibility filtering, then latency-based selection. Phase 1: a connector must be a member of a group associated with the Server Group referenced by the matching Application Segment, report CONNECTED to a Service Edge, and have a recent reachability probe showing the target alive. A sick connector or one that cannot reach the target is filtered out before assignment." The legacy doc itself notes the internal ordering and algorithm are not publicly published. The group-to-segment chain is sourced (see connector-groups); the filter order is not.

round-robin-setting.title: Effect of selectConnectorCloseToApp = false
round-robin-setting.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "If select_connector_close_to_app = false is set on a Server Group, selection is round-robin instead of latency-based." The setting is on application segments, not server groups (see segment-prefers-nearest-connector), and no registered source says what false does; the SDKs say only that it prefers nearest connector routing.

close-with-connector-failure-table.title: Reading a closed session by whether a connector was assigned
close-with-connector-failure-table.detail: Unverified legacy statement: a table mapping "LSS ConnectionStatus = Close, no Connector populated, no policy block" to every candidate being rejected by the eligibility filter, "Close with Connector populated and high ConnectionSetupTime" to a failure during the connection attempt, and "Open/Active with elevated ConnectionSetupTime/ServerSetupTime" to an eligible but slow connector, plus the advice to check whether a connector was assigned before suspecting the connector-to-app hop. The sourced finding is narrower: a zero connector ID also occurs for APP_NOT_REACHABLE and INVALID_DOMAIN (connector-id-zero), not only when no connector qualifies.
